title: Find your way with the black keys
summary: The black keys come in groups of two and three. That pattern is your map, and it leads you to C.

steps.title: The keyboard repeats
steps.body:
You already know the keys by feel. Theory just gives them names.

Look at the black keys. They come in **groups of two** and **groups of three**, over and over, all the way up the keyboard. That pattern is your map: every note name hangs off it.

steps.title: Groups of two and three
steps.body: Here is one group of two black keys and one group of three. The same pair of groups repeats in every part of the keyboard.

steps.title: C sits just left of the two
steps.body:
The white key just to the left of each group of two black keys is **C**. There is one in every repeat of the pattern, so a full 88-key piano has eight Cs.

The C nearest the middle of the keyboard, usually right under the brand name, is called **middle C**. It is the landmark everything else is measured from.

steps.title: Every C on the keyboard
steps.body: All eight Cs on an 88-key piano. Each one sits just left of a pair of black keys.

items.prompt: Play any C: look for a pair of black keys and take the white key just left of it.
Play a C in a different part of the keyboard.

steps.title: Free play
steps.body: Play anything you like. The app names each key as you press it. Watch for the Cs: each one sits just left of a pair of black keys.

items.prompt: Find a C near the top of the keyboard.
Find middle C without looking at the screen.
